text: Machine learning is a way for computers to learn from data without being explicitly programmed. One common type is supervised learning, where the computer uses labeled examples to understand patterns. These labeled examples, called training data, include both the input and the correct output. The computer analyzes this data to build a model—a kind of mathematical rule that captures the relationship. Once the model is ready, it can make predictions on new, unseen data. For instance, after training on photos of cats and dogs, the model can predict whether a new picture shows a cat or a dog. The quality of these predictions is measured by accuracy, which shows how often the model is correct. Better training data usually leads to higher accuracy.
